verdicts.evidence: p.7 §4.1.1: 'With KPTI, the lower-bound of the constant cost is on the order of 400–500 cycles'; 'Writing to CR3 is expensive, costing around 200 cycles'; footnote 1 method.

fix.protocol: KPTI constant cost measured by comparing an empty system call with and without the KPTI patch, measuring cycles spent in the MMU TLB miss handler, and subtracting that increase from the overall latency increase (footnote 1). HP DL160 G9 server, Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3 2.40 GHz, 128 GB DDR4 1866 MHz; Ubuntu-configured Linux kernels 3.0 to 4.20. The paper's general LEBench method (10,000 repetitions, K-best K=5, 5% tolerance) is described for its microbenchmarks; the paper does not say it was applied to this empty-system-call figure.
fix.conditions: Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3, Linux with KPTI (introduced after 4.14), with or without PCID; the lower bound of KPTI's constant cost per kernel entry and exit is 'on the order of 400–500 cycles'; value 400 = low end of that range; mainly two CR3 writes of around 200 cycles each.

verdicts.conditionsFr: Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3, Linux avec KPTI (introduit après la 4.14), avec ou sans PCID ; la borne basse du coût constant de KPTI par entrée et sortie du noyau est « de l’ordre de 400 à 500 cycles » ; la valeur 400 est le bas de cette plage ; coût dominé par deux écritures de CR3 d’environ 200 cycles chacune.
verdicts.conditionsEn: Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3, Linux with KPTI (introduced after 4.14), with or without PCID; the lower bound of KPTI's constant cost per kernel entry and exit is 'on the order of 400–500 cycles'; value 400 = low end of that range; mainly two CR3 writes of around 200 cycles each.
verdicts.notes: Value is the low end of an approximate range that is itself a lower bound; stated in conditions. Protocol fix: LEBench K-best method not stated for this figure; KPTI footnote method kept.

verdicts.evidence: p.7: 'For the shortest read test with a baseline latency of 344ns, the PCID optimization reduces the slowdown from 113% to 47%.' Fig. 3: slowdown with increasing baseline latency.

fix.protocol: LEBench read test, page cache warmed before measurement, each measurement repeated 10,000 times and reported with the K-best method (K=5, 5% tolerance). HP DL160 G9 server, Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3 2.40 GHz, 128 GB DDR4 1866 MHz; Ubuntu-configured Linux kernels 3.0 to 4.20.
fix.conditions: LEBench read test with the shortest baseline latency in Figure 3 (read slowdown due to KPTI vs baseline latency), Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3; baseline without KPTI = 344 ns; KPTI slowdown 113% without PCID, 47% with PCID.

verdicts.labelEn: Latency of the shortest read() test without KPTI (Xeon E5-2630 v3)

verdicts.conditionsEn: LEBench read test with the shortest baseline latency in Figure 3 (read slowdown due to KPTI vs baseline latency), Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3; baseline without KPTI = 344 ns; KPTI slowdown 113% without PCID, 47% with PCID.
verdicts.notes: Conditions fix: the paper does not say the shortest read test is a single 4 kB page nor tie the baseline to a '4.14-era' kernel; 'shortest' refers to baseline latency (Fig. 3). Protocol fix: KPTI footnote removed (not relevant).
